transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I'm struggling with these constant, overwhelming worries about germs and contamination. It's gotten so bad that I'm forced to wash my hands and clean things repeatedly, and it's completely taking over my daily life.
Besides your worries about germs and cleaning, do you also find yourself constantly worrying about many other everyday things, such as your finances, work, or family?
No, I don't really worry about everyday things like my finances, work, or family. My main concerns are almost completely focused on germs, contamination, and keeping things clean.
How much time would you say you spend each day dealing with these thoughts about germs and performing your cleaning rituals?
I'm not completely sure of the exact hours since I've never actually timed it. But it definitely feels like it takes up a massive, exhausting portion of my day from the moment I wake up.
Do you feel like these thoughts about germs are intrusive and unwanted, and do you perform the cleaning rituals mainly to relieve the intense anxiety they cause?

Yes, absolutely. The thoughts about germs feel incredibly intrusive and unwanted, and I just can't seem to get them out of my head. I only do the washing and cleaning because the anxiety gets so intense, and performing those rituals is the only way to get some temporary relief.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms of intrusive, unwanted thoughts about contamination (obsessions) and repetitive, time-consuming cleaning rituals to relieve anxiety (compulsions) are highly characteristic of Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder. The patient denies generalized worries about everyday life, ruling out GAD. The diagnosis of OCD is now confirmed, and no further questioning is required.
